title: Launch Gateway Heuristics and Economic Slate
content:
Purpose:
This is a living product-ops playbook for the "launch gateway" — the set of readiness heuristics, economic tradeoffs, and KPI signal flows that determine go/no-go, rollout cadence, and fallback behavior for feature launches that materially affect inference cost, latency, or regional capacity.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: product-ops, product managers, SRE, serving-runtime, solutions engineering, and sales engineering for dedicated/private customers.
- Scope: covers pre-launch gating, canary-to-scale cadence, KPI thresholds (latency, error, cost), economic decision heuristics, surge-runbook snippets, and open questions. Not an exhaustive ops runbook — see linked Confluence for runbook wiring.

Why a "gateway" approach:
- We want a compact, repeatable decision surface for launches that impact inference economics: small changes (prompt template tweaks) should use lighter gates; heavy changes (model variant, quantization, routing policy) need full gateway review.
- The gateway balances: user experience (latency/p99), unit cost (tokens / hour), and operational risk (error rates, capacity headroom).

Quick glossary:
- Gateway phase: alpha/canary -> phased -> scale
- Economic slate: quick cost delta estimates used at decision points
- SLO guard: thresholds tied to auto-fallback and manual escalation

Heuristics (decision shortcuts):
1) If user-facing latency p95 increases > 20% relative to baseline and p99 > 500ms then escalate to SRE and hold rollout.
2) If 1k-request-sample error rate > 0.8% in canary, abort and investigate (not a slow-roll).
3) If estimated cost delta for production traffic > 30% of current spend for that route, require dedicated capacity pre-commit conversation.
4) If model quantization reduces quality metric (eval prompts) by > 1.5% absolute, block until compensating changes (prompt/temperature) or retune.

KPI signal table (primary signals we watch during gateway):
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (ms) — by route and by model variant.
- Error rate (%) — by HTTP 5xx + model fallbacks.
- Token cost per 1k user tokens (USD) — platform-estimate for given quantization + batch.
- Throughput (requests/s) and GPU utilization (%) — per cluster/pool.
- Quality regressions — eval-set pass rate (%) and open user-reported quality tickets.
- Adoption delta — daily active users hitting new route (DAU share).

Thresholds (starter values — tune per product):
- Canary window length: 30–90 minutes or 10k requests, whichever comes first.
- Canary fraction: 1–3% traffic.
- Phased: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 24–72h with health checks at each step.
- Latency: p95 < baseline * 1.2 and p99 < 650ms for hosted API; for Dedicated, p95 < baseline * 1.15 and p99 < 600ms.
- Error: 5xx rate < 0.5% during canary; < 0.3% at phased steps.
- Cost: unit-cost increase < 20% allowed for feature that improves retention/engagement; otherwise require product signoff and finance review.

Economic slate (how to produce quick cost delta):
- Inputs: current route QPS, average tokens per request, baseline cost per 1k tokens, quantization multiplier (e.g., int8 -> -35% compute cost), expected batching uplift.
- Quick calc template (manual):
  - baseline_unit_cost = $0.12 per 1k tokens (example)
  - tokens_per_req = 45 (sample)
  - QPS = 12 -> daily_req = QPS * 86400
  - new_unit_cost = baseline_unit_cost * (1 + delta_percent)
  - daily_cost_delta = daily_req * tokens_per_req/1000 * (new_unit_cost - baseline_unit_cost)
- Output: present decimals and % delta along with sensitivity for +/- 10% tokens and +/- 15% QPS.

Readiness checklist (pre-canary):
[ ] Technical owners designated and on-call window assigned (names + pager)
[ ] Baseline metrics snapshot captured (p50/p95/p99, error, unit-cost)
[ ] Economical slate computed and finance informed if > 15% delta
[ ] Canary route created with feature-flag and auto-fallback to stable model variant
[ ] Alerting thresholds provisioned and smoke dashboards linked in runbook
[ ] Eval-set run showing no quality regression > 1% absolute
[ ] Playbook for rollback clearly documented with expected rollback time < 5min

Canary run playbook (ops run notes):
- Start canary at low-traffic period if possible.
- Observe first 5 minutes for immediate 5xx spikes, then 30-minute window for steady-state metrics.
- If p99 latency climbs and sustains > threshold, flip fallback and open SRE incident.
- Log: note user cohort (internal vs external), geo distribution, model variant ID, batch size config.

Surge and capacity fallback plan (short):
- If QPS > 2x expected during phased rollout: switch routing policy to lower-capacity model variant (quantized) or redirect to dedicated pool if pre-wired.
- For dedicated customers: pre-negotiated burst token to allow 10% traffic at baseline latency; escalation to sales/SE for re-contract within 24h.

Communication matrix: who broadcasts what and when:
- Canary start: product-ops -> slack #prodops (timestamp, fraction, owners)
- Canary healthy -> product mailing list + customer success if impacted customers in segment
- Canary fail -> incident channel + weekly postmortem assignment

Rollout economics scenarios (short example):
- Scenario A: small quality boost, cost +12% unit. Decision: phased rollout with 10%->50% over 48h; finance notified but no capex.
- Scenario B: large model bump, cost +40% unit. Decision: block on gateway until dedicated commit or selective routing for high-value customers only.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- How to automate the economic-slate calc in console? (linked artifact: CONFLUENCE)
- Add a standard heatmap in dashboard for combined cost x latency x quality risk.
- Agree on default canary fraction across teams (ops + serving-runtime tension). Current riff: 2% for hosted, 1% for global private.
- Define a lightweight legal/ compliance check for private deployments when model variants change inference behavior (PII-sensitive prompts).

Quick reference: owner roster for gateway decisions
- Gateway lead (product-ops): Maya Thompson (owner)
- SRE contact: Omar Li
- Serving-runtime: Caleb Nguyen
- Customer Success escalation: Priya Shah
- Finance advisor (cost delta > 20%): Hannah Ruiz

Notes and working ideas (informal):
- Consider a new boolean "economic-block" flag in rollout config: if true and projected cost delta > threshold, block automated staged rollout until manual approval.
- Small experiments: run A/B where A uses caching=on, B uses caching=off to measure real cost/latency tradeoffs on representative traffic.
- We should store a snapshot of eval-set results per model-commit as part of launch metadata for retrospective analysis.

Appendix: quick canned commands for the gateway starter kit (ops):
- Capture baseline: ./scripts/capture-baseline --route <route> --window 24h --out baseline.json
- Run economic-slate: ./tools/econ-slate --baseline baseline.json --tokens-per-req 45 --qps 12 --delta 0.35
- Canary flip: ./rollout/flip-canary --route <route> --frac 0.02 --owner maya@redwood.ai

End notes: this doc is deliberately minimalist and decision-focused. Link more exhaustive playbooks in Confluence and embed the economic-slate calc into Console ASAP.

Last quick checklist before I hand to SRE for review:
- [ ] Confirm alerting runbook paths in Ops (pager names)
- [ ] Add a one-paragraph customer impact blurb for CS to use if canary fails
- [ ] Wire the econ-slate to an automated slack notif when projected cost delta > 10%

-- Maya T. (product-ops)
